scope: didactic and ethical texts concerned with living conduct
project_definition_of_book_of_living.historical_anchor: Modern scholarship notes that a considerable part of Book of the Dead material had non-mortuary or temple uses and belonged to a broader priestly knowledge pool associated with temple archives and the House of Life.

strongest_new_starting_node.source_summary: In the Spell 113 tradition, Horus's severed hands/arms are cast into the water; Sobek uses a net to retrieve them, and Isis restores them to their proper place.
strongest_new_starting_node.claim_boundary: This is not a text about Kem or the lost phallus of Osiris; it is an ancient body-part recovery/restoration motif whose structure resembles the modern creative story.

book_of_dead_transition_nodes.bridge_to_living: After restoration, conflict is calmed and ordered relations become possible.
Explicitly shifts the peace motif toward those who are living.
Family restoration becomes a natural transition to father-to-son instruction traditions.

high_value_passages: Ptahhotep advises restraint in answering a fiery opponent and describes peace following a storm.
The text says that planting love brings sustenance.
It explicitly says that every person teaches by deeds and that the lesson is passed from children to their children.
It presents teaching from the past so the next generation can become an example.
book_of_living_continuation_hits.kem_relevance: Strong functional resonance with KEM = EXAMPLE_NOT_AUTHORITY.
Very strong ethical resonance with helping without requiring kingship or reward.

book_of_living_continuation_hits.text: Teaching of a Man for his Son

institutional_bridge.book_of_dead_side: Oxford Handbook research describes Book of the Dead and temple decoration as drawing on a broader priestly knowledge pool; the House of Life was involved in collecting/codifying material.
institutional_bridge.book_of_living_side: The Onomasticon of Amenemipet identifies its compiler as a scribe of divine books in the House of Life and frames the teaching as knowledge of what exists in the world.

janus_interpretation.strongest_observation: The cleanest cross-corpus transition is not an identical repeated plot but a functional handoff: funerary/religious texts restore bodies, continuity and divine peace; wisdom texts then teach how humans should preserve order through restraint, truth, kindness, example and intergenerational transmission.
janus_interpretation.kem_position: Kem maps more naturally to the living-side ethic of example than to any ancient deity-role.
janus_interpretation.set_position: The modern Set arc remains creative; ancient texts distribute planning, mediation and order among several figures rather than assigning the full modern role to Set.
janus_interpretation.parallel_world_model: Allowed only as a fictional comparison heuristic: event functions may remain stable while names, agents, sequence and objects drift.
not_proven: that the two corpora were intended as one continuous hidden narrative
that the modern JANUS story was encoded or predicted
that another universe caused textual similarities
that Kem is an ancient attested person

negative_controls.contrast: Contains strong distrust/fear and advice not to trust friends or brothers in one section, which runs against the Kem/family-reunion ethic.
negative_controls.reason_for_retention: Prevents cherry-picking Egyptian wisdom as uniformly supporting the modern story.

negative_controls.contrast: Many traditions retain violent Horus-Set conflict, defeat and coercion.
negative_controls.reason_for_retention: Peace passages are one strand, not the whole Egyptian tradition.
